journey:kim-ki-chang-life-of-jesus.t: The Life of Jesus (series of 30 paintings)
journey:kim-ki-chang-life-of-jesus.l: Seoul Museum, Buam-dong, Seoul, South Korea
journey:kim-ki-chang-life-of-jesus.m: Ink and colour (traditional East Asian painting)
journey:kim-ki-chang-life-of-jesus.noimg: © Estate of Kim Ki-chang. The series is held by the Seoul Museum in Buam-dong, Seoul.

x.summary: Painted while Kim was a refugee during the Korean War, these thirty scenes retell the life of Christ from the Annunciation to the Ascension as if it had happened in Joseon-dynasty Korea. Jesus and the apostles wear white hanbok and horsehair gat hats, and Gospel events unfold among thatched villages and pine-clad hills. The series is a landmark of Korean Christian art and of Christian inculturation in East Asia.
facts: Kim, who lost his hearing in childhood, began the series in 1952 at his mother-in-law's house in Gunsan, where he had fled during the war.

He was encouraged by an American missionary, Anders K. Jensen, who argued that Koreans needed an image of Jesus that looked like them; Kim adapted traditional European Christian iconography to Korean settings.
In the 1970s Kim painted the official standard portrait of King Sejong the Great, the image used on the South Korean 10,000-won banknote.
